**Potential issues:**

- "But we did not go to sleep without some little chat." — Absent in draft. Minor, transitional.
- The middle passage: "I thought this indifference of his very strange. But savages are strange beings; at times you do not know exactly how to take them. At first they are overawing; their calm self-collectedness of simplicity seems a Socratic wisdom." — The draft has "Savages are strange beings. At first they are overawing; their calm self-collectedness of simplicity seems a Socratic wisdom." — present but slightly condensed, acceptable.
- The repetition in the draft of "content with his own companionship; always equal to himself" appears twice (once in the compressed middle paragraph, once verbatim from the Cape Horn passage). This is a drafting artifact but not a source-text loss.
- "I had noticed also that Queequeg never consorted at all, or but very little, with the other seamen in the inn. He made no advances whatever; appeared to have no desire to enlarge the circle of his acquaintances. All this struck me as mighty singular; yet, upon second thoughts, there was something almost sublime in it." — The "something almost sublime in it" interpretive note is absent/flattened in the draft.
- The detail "perhaps a little complimented" after Queequeg asks to be bedfellows — absent. Minor.
- "considering the affectionate arm I had found thrown over me upon waking in the morning" — absent. Minor.

The "something almost sublime in it" loss is notable — it's Ishmael's interpretive pivot before the Cape Horn reflection, and its absence flattens a key moment. But it's not culturally famous or critically canonical at signature level; it's medium at best.

No high-severity losses found. The major signatures are all preserved. I count roughly two medium-severity issues (the "almost sublime" pivot and the duplicate text artifact that slightly muddles the narrative flow), plus a few low items.
